title: Control plane resource graph + CRUD design notes
content:
Purpose: capture a compact, pragmatic design for the control-plane data model that treats resources (models, endpoints, pools), environments, regions and clusters as a resource graph, and a corresponding CRUD surface that supports multi-region routing policies, capacity-aware scheduling, and eventual consistency semantics.

Context + motivation:
- Current sketches focus on flat resources per-cluster. We need a graph-first view to support: routing fallbacks, cross-region KV/cache of prefixes, and explicit affinities for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Primary consumers: routing service, scheduler (placement), control plane UI/rollouts, billing/quotas.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Single source of truth for resource topology (nodes=resources/environments/regions/clusters, edges=owns/located_in/peers).
2) Lightweight CRUD with optimistic concurrency and per-entity versioning to avoid long locks across regions.
3) Routing policy DSL that compiles to a scored list of candidate clusters/regions + deterministic tiebreakers.
4) Fast reads locally (cache with TTL, watch-based invalidation) and safe writes that can be retried without violating invariants.
5) Clear ownership and audit metadata for enterprise customers (who can modify route policies / pin model versions).

Core entities (proposal):
- Resource (type: model | endpoint | pool | job): id (uuid v4), name, owner_team, visibility (public/private/customer-owned), version_tag, created_at, updated_at, metadata (free-form tags).
- Environment: id, name (dev/stage/prod/custom), region_selector (e.g. [us-west-2, eu-west-1] or expression), cluster_selector (optional), default_routing_policy_id (nullable).
- Region: id, name, cloud_region_code (aws:us-west-2), geo (NA/EU/APAC), capacity_metrics_ref (pointer), prefer_local boolean.
- Cluster: id, name, region_id, capacity_profile (gpu_count, mem_gb, instance_type_family), labels, status (active/draining/maintenance), last_heartbeat.
- RoutingPolicy: id, name, owner, priority, rules[] (DSL - see below), fallback_policy_id (nullable), created_at, updated_at, version.
- ResourceAssignment/Placement (edge entity): id, resource_id, cluster_id, weight, state (provisioned/allocated/evicted), pinned_version (optional), last_update, lease_expiry (nullable).

Notes on IDs and versioning:
- All primary entities get UUID v4. Additionally, each entity carries a monotonic integer revision and an etag string (hash of payload + revision) to support optimistic update semantics.
- Revision increments on any mutating change. Clients must provide last_seen_revision to perform conditional updates (HTTP If-Match via ETag).

Routing policy DSL (high level):
- A routing policy is a prioritized list of clauses. Each clause is either a filter expression (region==eu* && cluster.labels.gpu==true) and a scoring function (latency_score * weight + capacity_score * weight2).
- Example rule: {when: (request.latency_sla < 150), filter: region in [us-west-2, us-east-1] && cluster.labels.fast-network, score: (1.0 - normalized_latency) * 0.7 + normalized_available_slots * 0.3}
- Compile step: DSL -> list of candidate clusters with final score. Sort by (priority, score, deterministic tie-breaker: cluster_id).
- Fallback chain: policy may reference a fallback_policy_id; router walks chain until candidate found.

CRUD API surface (RESTish; aim for uniformity):
- GET /v1/resources?type=model&env=prod - list with server-side paging (cursor) and optional projection fields.
- POST /v1/resources - create resource. Payload: {name, type, owner_team, visibility, metadata}. Returns 201 + Location + body with id + etag + revision.
- GET /v1/resources/{id} - read single resource (query param include_placements=true to fetch assignments).
- PATCH /v1/resources/{id} - partial update. Requires If-Match: etag header if not forcing. Returns new etag + revision.
- DELETE /v1/resources/{id} - logical delete (tombstone: deleted_at). Hard delete admin-only with grace period.

- Environments: analogous CRUD; special routes to bind/unbind regions: POST /v1/environments/{id}/regions -> body region_ids[]; server validates overlaps and selector conflicts.

- Clusters: cluster creation is restricted (platform-only) but readable. POST /v1/clusters/register (internal) with signed token. PATCH /v1/clusters/{id}/status for heartbeat.

- Routing policies: POST /v1/routing-policies (owner teams can create), GET list, PATCH when editing rules. Policy edits produce new revision; routers should tombstone old policy but keep revisions for audit.

- Placements: POST /v1/placements -> body {resource_id, cluster_id, desired_weight, pin_version}. This creates ResourceAssignment. DELETE /v1/placements/{id} evicts. Placements are the primary way scheduler and control plane communicate desired allocations.

API semantics and consistency model:
- Strong read-after-write is not feasible cross-region. Pattern: clients operate with optimistic updates + etags. Write path uses a single-region control plane leader per resource shard (shard by resource_id % N) to provide linearizable updates for that shard.
- Reads: prefer local cache; if stale flag returned then client may retry with consistent=true to go to leader.
- Conflicts: server returns 409 with server_revision and diff-hint. Client best practice: fetch, re-apply patch, retry with If-Match.

Multi-region concerns and placements:
- Placement decisions must consider: capacity, node labels, customer region preferences, regulatory constraints (data residency), network latency, cost (spot vs reserved). We should keep cost as a scoring input but not as a hard constraint at first.
- Dual-write anti-pattern: avoid simultaneous edits from different regions. Use leader-shard mapping (deterministic by resource_id) so writes route to same region leader. Control plane should be able to relocate leader mapping for HA with safe resync.

Cluster affinity and leases:
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, we support pinned assignments: ResourceAssignment.pinned_version and lease_expiry. Lease semantics: default short lease (5m) for ephemeral allocations, longer for pinned. Leases help cleanup if cluster disappears (eviction after lease expiry + backoff).

Cache & watches for routing service:
- Router instances maintain an in-memory view of relevant entities: resources, placements, clusters, policies. Subscribe to change feed (pub/sub) from control plane (region-local) and reconcile periodically (leader-checkpoint + TTL).
- Misses: router can fall back to calling /v1/resources/{id}?consistent=true to get leader-verified state.

Operational notes and migration plan (from existing flat schema):
- Phase 0: implement new entities minimally (RoutingPolicy, ResourceAssignment) in backend with dual-write shim that populates both old and new tables.
- Phase 1: switch read paths for routing service to new graph API in read-only mode; validate behavior under load; collect metrics.
- Phase 2: flip write paths for placements + policy edits to write-only to new model; run canary.
- Phase 3: deprecate old tables, enable GC of tombstoned rows after 90 days.

Example curl snippets (for UX teams):
- Create policy:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    https://api.redwood/v1/routing-policies -d '{"name":"prefer-local-low-latency","owner":"serving-team","priority":10,"rules":[{"filter":"region==request.region","score":"0.9*latency_score + 0.1*capacity"}],"fallback_policy_id":null}'

- Place a resource into a cluster:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"resource_id":"<uuid>","cluster_id":"c-123","desired_weight":1}' https://api.redwood/v1/placements

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- DSL: do we standardize on a JSON expression tree (safer for compile) vs a small declarative language (friendlier)?
- How to express hard regulatory constraints vs soft preferences? Separate clause types? Tagging?
- Leader-shard sizing: how many shards (N) should we target? 256? 1024? tradeoffs: reshard cost vs contention.
- Migration safety: timeline for tombstone windows, and metrics to watch when flipping reads.

Testing checklist (to validate design):
- Unit: entity create/update/delete with etag/revision behavior; conflict simulation.
- Integration: router rollouts reading from cache vs consistent reads; fallback chain behavior.
- Chaos: cluster heartbeat loss; placement lease expiry; leader resharding while edits in flight.
- Perf: large-scale listing requests across thousands of resources; router reconcile QPS.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Share this doc with placement and routing owners, ask for concrete scoring functions from scheduling team.
- Prototype a small in-memory implementation to validate DSL compilation and tie-breaking behavior within 2 weeks.
- Add explicit sample JSON schemas in a follow-up doc (separate file) and map fields to DB columns / indexes.

References and links:
- Confluence design index (linked above) for older sketches.
- Jira PLAT-789: placement refactor epic (contains state machine diagrams).
- GitHub PR GHP-1234: initial ResourceAssignment table patch.

Bottom line: aim for graph-first, optimistic-concurrency CRUD API with small, composable routing policies that compile to deterministic candidate lists. Keep read paths fast with caches and watches and keep writes sharded to a leader to avoid cross-region races.

Unresolved: owner for the DSL internal representation (scheduling vs routing teams).
